annotations.annotation_text: Oneiric dimension "night" on page 7 ("The Fall of Finnegan"): the nocturnal consciousness surfaces within the mythic fall of Tim Finnegan / HCE, the thunderclap awakening primitive religion, and the recumbent giant embedded in the Dublin landscape. During this Age of Gods (Theocratic) phase, Joyce reconstructs the sleeping body's sensory deprivation — dimmed sight, distorted hearing, dream-logic association — transforming somatic experience into polyphonic language.
sources: Bishop, John. Joyce's Book of the Dark. https://archive.org/details/joycesbookofdark0000bish
Freud, Sigmund. The Interpretation of Dreams. https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/4349
Troy, Mark L. Mummeries of Resurrection. http://www.rosenlake.net

annotations.annotation_text: Fall/resurrection motif "wall" on page 7 ("The Fall of Finnegan"): Tim Finnegan tumbling from his ladder, Humpty Dumpty shattering from the wall, Adam falling in Eden — all converge within the mythic fall of Tim Finnegan / HCE, the thunderclap awakening primitive religion, and the recumbent giant embedded in the Dublin landscape. The comic-cosmic Fall during the Age of Gods (Theocratic) phase demands its counterpart: resurrection through the whiskey-splash of the water of life (uisce beatha).
sources: The Ballad of Tim Finnegan's Wake. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finnegan%27s_Wake
Atherton, James S. The Books at the Wake. https://archive.org/details/booksatwake0000athe
Opie, Iona and Peter. The Oxford Dictionary of Nursery Rhymes. https://archive.org/details/oxforddictionary0000unse_m4u1
